name: thinking-waiting
prompt:
Create a production KEY POSE board for an animated desktop puppy, NOT a full animation sprite sheet. Use the two attached images as strict identity/style references. Exact same apricot puppy, cream forehead blaze/muzzle/chest/paws/tail tip, brown floppy ears, sage collar and ROUND gold tag. Keep original soft shaded cartoon line style, face/head/body/leg proportions and 3/4 view facing right. No redesign or added accessories.
Layout: exactly 8 separate FULL BODY drawings in a regular 4 column by 2 row grid on a truly TRANSPARENT background. Large clear transparent gutters. Same fixed camera and same character scale across every cell; paws on the same floor line. No text, numbers, grid lines, background, shadows, props, cut off tails, extra legs or human gestures.
Top row contains THINKING key poses, from left to right: (1) original calm seated pose with all paws grounded; (2) whole puppy still seated, head tilts noticeably about 16 degrees left, eyes look thoughtfully up-right, floppy ears follow gravity, mouth closed; (3) still seated, head tilts about 12 degrees the other way, curious attentive eyes look up-left, natural weight shift in neck only; (4) head comes near center and slightly down with a slow blink, paws remain grounded. Keep full character anatomy continuous, do not detach the head or rotate a cut-out.
Bottom row contains WAITING FOR A HUMAN key poses: (5) seated puppy leans its weight onto the FAR front leg, NEAR front paw just begins to lift; (6) NEAR front paw is gently folded and held below the collar, rounded canine paw facing downward, far paw planted, calm expectant eye contact; (7) same held paw at exactly same height, head leans slightly toward viewer 6 degrees, patient friendly expression, tail resting; (8) same held paw, head back to center, eyes softly closed mid-blink. No waving or begging with two paws. All four bottom drawings must share exactly the same stable body proportions, collar position and supporting paw location. Anatomical dog legs, no elbows attached to cheeks, no fingers.
These 8 images will be stable key poses for optical-flow interpolation; prioritize identity and coherent forms over adding detail. Image 1 is the master identity; image 2 shows approved pose/style range.

name: complete
prompt:
Create a production KEY POSE board for ONE short joyful puppy completion animation. Use the attached character anchor and approved pose board as strict identity and art style references. Exact same apricot puppy with cream forehead blaze/muzzle/chest/paws/tail tip, floppy brown ears, sage collar and ROUND gold tag. Preserve face/head size relative to body, coat markings, line thickness and shading. This is the SAME dog in all images, no redesign.
Exactly 8 isolated FULL BODY key drawings, regular 4 columns x 2 rows, read left to right then next row. Transparent background with wide clear gutters. Fixed 3/4 camera facing right and constant scale, same floor baseline in every cell; ensure tails/ears/all feet fully fit. No text/numbers/grid/props/shadows/sparkles/speed marks or background.
A natural canine celebration, no jumping or standing upright like a person:
1. Seated like original master, head brightens into a happy open mouth smile, tiny pink tongue, tail lifts.
2. Puppy leans its chest forward to start standing, rear legs begin extending, front paws stay on floor.
3. Standing on all four legs, one natural short step forward by the NEAR forepaw, cheerful face, head remains same size.
4. Front elbows bending and forepaws reaching forward as puppy starts a playful bow, hindquarters remain up, tail curls up.
5. Full PLAY BOW: chest close to floor, front legs stretched out with both paws flat, hindquarters up over bent rear legs, head lifted looking happily at viewer, same head proportions, no detached legs.
6. Chest rises halfway back from bow, paws push against floor, tail sways to the other side naturally, happy relaxed ears.
7. Puppy sits back down, four canine paws/legs correctly attached, head happy and relaxed, tail gives a last short wag.
8. Back to original content seated posture with mouth gently closed and all paws grounded, tail returning to original position.
Make the body posture changes clear and anatomically believable, with actual shoulder/spine/hip relations, not a rotated pasted torso. Keep character identity consistent across all 8 KEY POSES; in-between animation frames will be computed separately.
